reason: Episode executed this five-step diagnostic flow to audit SuaraNetijen's on-page SEO (34/100 score). Data from 4 sources (RankMySEO, curl raw HTML, Inertia props, Google Autocomplete) cross-referenced to isolate SSR as root cause of all on-page failures. This methodology is reusable for any SPA/Inertia SEO audit.

Session diagnosed a GSC noindex-excluded spike (155 -> 2,637) as caused by indexable /search browse and related-entities blocks linking thin noindex entity pages. The methodology skill has no step for excluded-by-noindex diagnosis; adding it as a sixth triangulation point.

Episode showed the RankMySEO score (34/100, audit dated 1 Oct, pre-SSR) stayed flat while GSC impressions rose 25→525 and position improved 33.7→10.3; the skill lacked a step for stale third-party audits, a check that the noindex fix was pushed before claiming it live, and a sorted-input note for comm.
Adds the triangulation case for a flat third-party SEO score against improving GSC data, so the next session reads the score as lagging rather than failing.

Episode fixed noindex links from the category page fallback, then sweep still found 8 noindex targets across /top/technology, /top/digital-services, /top/fmcg and /. The fallback-period mismatch is a reusable diagnostic for SPA listings linking to threshold-gated pages.

RankMySEO audit fixes this episode surfaced concrete, reusable rules (starter page cap, noindex-link false blocks, title suffix rule, email_off via v-html, thin-page copy rule that the user corrected, live word-count method) that the SEO methodology skill lacked.
The description index line did not name the audit-finding vocabulary a user actually types (RankMySEO, blocked from indexing, thin pages), so the skill would not route on those prompts.

Episode verified SSR for new /contact page and entity JSON-LD; hit three traps (page cache froze CSR fallback after SSR was down, pending migrations gave 500 mistaken for SSR issue, Vite manifest missing for new page). Also recorded owner decisions for trust-page publisher identity and reply SLA as copy rules for this SEO work.
Episode fixed Fase A audit findings and then requested indexing in GSC. Skill lacked a post-deploy indexing step and the sitemap/footer link precondition for new trust pages.
Episode requested GSC indexing for changed trust pages after deploy. The skill had no post-deploy indexing step, so the choice of URLs, quota handling, and what to report was improvised.

Episode re-checked RankMySEO rows against live HTML: title row was stale (live 45-60 chars vs audit 168), and blocked-from-indexing rows were intentional noindex on below-threshold entities and no-ranking top lists. Existing step 8 lacked both guards, so a future session could "fix" a stale or intentional finding.
Episode found 26 thin /top/* rows in the audit but only 11 were in the sitemap and indexable; scoping to sitemap first avoids wasted copy work on noindex pages.
GSC 404s on purged entity URLs were investigated and resolved with no code change; recording the check prevents a wrong redirect or code hunt next time.

A parallel 8-request sweep plus a 5-minute page cache made 38 sitemap pages serve an empty shell to crawlers (26 Oct). Step 9 covers local SSR verification only; production sweep method and the cache-hit reading were missing.

The first hypothesis for Discovered/Crawled-not-indexed pages (`/banding/*` thin copy) was wrong; the sitemap-wide inbound-link check ruled out orphaning. The method (triage by URL status, then link median, then cache check) is not written anywhere in the skill.
Folded into seo-audit-and-metrics; the 11-step procedure is carried in references/audit-playbook.md.
